messages:
maria: Heads-up — after the bundle-merge at ~10:12 PT, consoles with multiple sparklines and SVG layers are showing ~400-800ms main-thread parse spikes. DevTools points at a new chunk. Anyone else seeing it?

alex: seeing it in canary. heatmap LCP up ~300ms. bundle diff shows +350KB gz. :frowning:

maria: repro steps: open dashboard with 6+ series, open Performance tab -> Timeline shows "Parse HTML" and "Evaluate Script" dominated by chunk `charts-svg-merge`. paste top lines below.

maria: ```
10:14.223 Parse HTML 120ms
10:14.350 Evaluate Script (charts-svg-merge.js) 420ms
10:14.780 Layout -> Recalculate Style 60ms
```

kevin: the merge pulled in a helper from viz-utils that inlines a bunch of defs into each sparkline. looks like duplicated SVG template code per series. i can PR a dedupe, but we should rollback to stop the canary impact.

julia: could the routing-weight tweak from earlier (09:50) be amplifying this? we bumped canary routing so more traffic hits the new bundle — both changes together might explain the spike.

sam: FYI deploy-bot: canary-deploy 2024-06-19T17:12Z -> charts-svg-merge (attached).

deploy-bot: deploy success for charts-svg-merge @maria @alex :white_check_mark:

alex: quick debug: telemetry init now does top-level imports which increases parse cost. it's client-side and runs synchronously. lazy-init or deferring telemetry init would help.

maria: proposal: 1) rollback the merge immediately 2) follow-up to lazy-load/dedupe SVG templates at build-time 3) add a canary perf gate for multi-series dashboards. agree?

kevin: +1 for rollback. i'll open a revert PR now.

julia: also suggest a soft mitigation: add a routing quota safeguard that lowers prefetch/concurrent charts if the client parse time spikes for a route. temporary but buys time.

sam: created PR #4512 (revert) and issue #4520 for dedupe/lazy-load. link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ui/pull/4512

maria: thanks — monitoring. canary should stabilize in ~10m after the revert. if not, we'll escalate and route users to a lightweight chart variant server-side.

alex: thanks all, ping me for canary smoke or if you want me to help with lazy-init patch.
